stories.title: Sudan: 'Unbearable Hardship' in Sudan - - Displaced People in Kordofan Eat Animal Feed to Avert Starvation
stories.summary: Sudan: 'Unbearable Hardship' in Sudan - - Displaced People in Kordofan Eat Animal Feed to Avert Starvation 13 August 2026 Dabanga (Port Sudan) Ed Daein / El Obeid — Humanitarian activist Huweida Abdelrahman Saleh has described desperate conditions in Ed Daein locality in West Kordofan, where hunger has driven some families to eat ambaz , amid a sharp rise in grain prices. A malwa of millet now costs SDG 20,000, while sources of income have disappeared and humanitarian aid has struggled to reach the area. El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, is experiencing a severe deterioration in health and basic services, acute water shortages, and a huge influx of displaced people into shelter centres. Ambaz , which has become a food source for displaced people in Ed Daein, is the residue of sesame and groundnut seeds left after oil has been extracted, and is normally used as animal feed. Saleh told Radio Dabanga that a team working on an emergency humanitarian response travelled to Ed Daein to distribute food baskets to 100 families.

stories.title: Africa: The Beijing of It All - Africa's Development Terms Are No Longer Written in Washington or Brussels
stories.summary: Africa: The Beijing of It All - Africa's Development Terms Are No Longer Written in Washington or Brussels 13 August 2026 African Arguments analysis By Wanjiku Wanjohi In the period that followed decolonisation, Africa's development landscape continued to be shaped by Western partnerships. By the late 1990s and early 2000s, this Western-facing architecture took the form of policy conditionality, governance agendas and institutional reform attached to rotating credit agreements. This approach rested, at least in part, on a simple reality: countries in the Global South had limited alternatives for accessing large-scale development financing. At the beginning of the twenty-first century, most foreign aid and investment flowing into Africa still came from Europe and North America. Explicit conditionality had become a defining feature of development cooperation, making this 'support' increasingly complicated for many African governments.

stories.title: Africa: African Rights Advocates Coordinate Response to Family Law Backlash
stories.summary: African Rights Advocates Coordinate Response to Family Law Backlash 13 August 2026 Inter Press Service By Chemtai Kirui Nairobi — Campaigners say anti-rights movements are increasingly using family law to challenge women's rights to inheritance, property, divorce and child custody. Women's rights advocates, judges and lawyers have launched a coordinated campaign to reform family laws that discriminate against women and girls in Africa. While the past decade has brought important legal advances in some countries, progress has also been marked by stagnation and backsliding. Increasingly, influential and often well-resourced and highly coordinated anti-rights actors are promoting regressive conservative ideologies that seek to repeal existing legal protections and obstruct reforms that would strengthen rights for women and girls. Family law governs some of the most consequential aspects of daily life, including marriage, divorce, child custody, inheritance and property rights.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Forced Conscription Resurfaces Across Oromia As Ethiopia Continues to Grapple With Security Crises
stories.summary: Ethiopia: Forced Conscription Resurfaces Across Oromia As Ethiopia Continues to Grapple With Security Crises 13 August 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) analysis Addis Abeba — Reports of forced conscription are resurfacing in several parts of Oromia, including the Sheger City area surrounding the capital Addis Abeba, with families alleging that young people have been taken against their will and, in some cases, that money has subsequently been demanded for their release. The latest accounts, gathered by Addis Standard from residents in East Hararghe and East Bale zones, come amid heightened security tensions across Ethiopia, including renewed confrontation between federal authorities and forces aligned with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the continuing conflict between federal forces and Fano fighters in Amhara region, and insecurity in parts Benishangul-Gumuz regional state. Two families interviewed by Addis Standard said relatives had disappeared after travelling outside their home areas. Their accounts could not be independently verified, and it was not immediately possible to establish whether those taken were recruited into the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF), regional militia structures, or another armed formation. A businessman from Mekenisa Kebele in Chinaksen, East Hararghe Zone of Oromia regional state, said his younger brother "disappeared for three days" while travelling to Dire Dawa City Administration last week to assist with his business.

China, the continent's largest foreign mine operator, and the US have been the most active in this regard, with their ongoing mining investment push supporting the development of concessions, railways, energy infrastructure, and other major projects. Nevertheless, there are concerns that this ongoing mineral push will subject African countries to the superpower rivalry between Beijing and Washington, with the US highlighting that its increased engagement in Africa is motivated by its intention to reduce Beijing's continental mineral dominance. Against this backdrop, there are allegations, notably from Zambia, that the US has conditioned the signing of bilateral health partnership agreements on ensuring access to US critical minerals. In parallel, despite being the continent's largest international mining investor, Chinese companies have been accused, including by labour unions and local media outlets, of poor worker treatment and importing Chinese labour for their projects.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
stories.summary: Image source, EPA By Tabby Wilson Published 13 August 2026 The current outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is on track to surpass the deadliest outbreak of the disease ever, the director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO) has said. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters that the 2026 outbreak, "at its current pace", would "eclipse" that of the 2014-2016 occurrence, which killed at least 11,000 people. The outbreak this year, declared on 15 May, has seen at least 4,300 cases and caused more than 2,000 deaths. The WHO said on Wednesday it hoped to reverse the spread of the disease within three months but warned that this meant bringing transmission under control - not ending the outbreak entirely. The epidemic was only officially declared in May, but it is believed the outbreak began at least three months before then, health officials said this week. "We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us," WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said at a news conference in the city of Bunia, near the centre of the outbreak.

stories.summary: Elvira Dyangani Ose, who directed Barcelona’s contemporary art museum, will succeed Koyo Kouoh at Zeitz MOCAA after she died suddenly last year from cancer.

stories.summary: RDC : autour de Tshisekedi, d’ultimes tractations en attendant la convocation du dialogue Alors que plusieurs sources évoquent une possible prise de parole du président Félix Tshisekedi dans les prochains jours, ce dernier a réuni des représentants des Églises et les membres d’une commission spéciale pour évoquer les contours des futures assises. Félix Tshisekedi reçoit une délégation des représentants de la Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo et de l’Église du Christ au Congo (Cenco-ECC), le 3 février 2025. © Présidence RDC Par Stanis Bujakera Tshiamala et Romain Gras Publié le 12 août à 14h11, modifié à 14h39 Lecture : 3 minutes. stories.summary: Présidentielle en Zambie : duel dans les urnes entre Hichilema, favori pour un second mandat, et Mundubile, opposant sous pression Favori des sondages, Hakainde Hichilema brigue un second mandat face à Brian Mundubile. stories.title: Zimbabwe : au moins 44 morts dans le chavirage d’un ferry sur le lac Kariba
stories.summary: D’une capacité de 90 personnes, le bateau comptait à son bord cinq membres d’équipages et 114 passagers adultes, selon le service de secours national. Les opérations de secours ont été compliquées par le mauvais temps.

stories.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
stories.summary: Passengers rescued from the ferry that capsized on Tuesday on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba. Photograph: Maxton Kanhema/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Passengers rescued from the ferry that capsized on Tuesday on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba. Photograph: Maxton Kanhema/AFP/Getty Images At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe , police said. The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales. A crew member told the national broadcaster ZBC that there were 153 people onboard when the ferry overturned on Tuesday after it hit large waves.

stories.title: Deported From the U.S., Trapped in a Prison in Africa
stories.summary: Roberto Mosquera, a Cuban immigrant who has lived in the United States since 1980 and completed a prison sentence in 1996, was arrested by ICE last year and sent to a prison in Eswatini, a country in Africa he’d never heard of. After a hunger strike, Mosquera obtained a phone and talked with Nicholas Casey of The New York Times Magazine to share what is happening there.

stories.title: Halting the march of the African armyworm: a natural cure offers hope to farmers
stories.summary: Finding dead African armyworms in a field set entomologist Letodi Luki Mathulwe on a path that may finally lead to a way to control the dreaded pest. Photograph: Letodi Luki Mathulwe View image in fullscreen Finding dead African armyworms in a field set entomologist Letodi Luki Mathulwe on a path that may finally lead to a way to control the dreaded pest. Photograph: Letodi Luki Mathulwe Halting the march of the African armyworm: a natural cure offers hope to farmers South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa. The white substance was a naturally occurring fungus and it was wiping out the caterpillar, which gained its name from its march-like advance through fields of crops.

stories.title: Zambia's 2026 election: Key issues to watch
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5IcdD Up to 8.7 million voters will decide whether Hichilema's economic reforms deserve another term Image: Moses Mwape/REUTERS Advertisement Zambia 's general election on Thursday will be fought on economic recovery, governance reforms and a sweeping change to the country's parliamentary map. Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema , leader of the United Party for National Development (UPND), is seeking a second term against 14 opponents. His principal challenger is Brian Mundubile, a former ally of the late President Edgar Lungu , who has surged to the front of a fragmented opposition after being backed by a coalition of rival parties. The Electoral Commission announced in April that 70 new constituencies would be added, raising the number of parliamentary seats from 156 to 226, creating smaller, more local voting districts. Up to 8.7 million voters are expected to take part in the elections, a majority of whom are women.

stories.title: Côte d’Ivoire :  Yacine Idriss Diallo unique candidat à la FIF, les clubs brandissent le boycott
stories.summary: La Fédération ivoirienne de football élira son président le 12 septembre, Yacine Idriss Diallo étant l’unique candidat, après des tractations gouvernementales. Mais la grogne couve chez les clubs, qui réclament plus de moyens.

stories.title: TotalEnergies, Eni, Shell… Comment la crise d’Ormuz profite aux majors, y compris en Afrique
stories.summary: Grâce à l’envol des cours et à la progression des marges de raffinage, les résultats financiers des géants des hydrocarbures sont en nette progression. Les cartes sont rebattues à l’échelle mondiale, et l’attractivité du continent augmente.

stories.title: Soudan : Khartoum visée par des frappes de drones des paramilitaires pour le deuxième jour de suite
stories.summary: Les paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide ont lancé mercredi une vaste attaque coordonnée de drones, visant la capitale et d’autres villes contrôlées par l’armée, distantes de plusieurs centaines de kilomètres.

stories.title: Cameroun : de Genève à Yaoundé, Samuel Mvondo Ayolo, gardien du temple Biya
stories.summary: Il est le directeur du cabinet civil de Paul Biya et, entre la Suisse, la France et le Cameroun, son bouclier pour contrer rumeurs et rivalités au sein du sérail. Portrait de Samuel Mvondo Ayolo, homme de l’ombre d’un président absent.

stories.title: Zambia Election: President Hichilema Faces Backlash Ahead of Vote
stories.summary: President Hakainde Hichilema was elected five years ago, promising to protect civil liberties in his copper-rich African nation. Now, he’s accused of trampling on them.

stories.title: Drowned the day her visa came through: the tragedy of a Moroccan footballer trying to reach Ceuta
stories.summary: Faten Omar Ben El Azizi, a 26-year-old football player in Morocco’s regional league, died with at least 141 others while trying to reach Ceuta. Photograph: Handout View image in fullscreen Faten Omar Ben El Azizi, a 26-year-old football player in Morocco’s regional league, died with at least 141 others while trying to reach Ceuta. Photograph: Handout Drowned the day her visa came through: the tragedy of a Moroccan footballer trying to reach Ceuta Struggling on her meagre pay, Faten Ben Omar El Azizi dreamed of reaching Europe. Then she joined thousands trying to reach a better life in Spain F ootball was the life Faten Ben Omar El Azizi had wanted. She had long played in Morocco’s regional league for Moghreb Atlético Tetuán, whose striking kit replicates the colours of the famous Spanish club Atlético Madrid.

stories.title: Ceuta showed just how easily Europe can be divided
stories.summary: Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters View image in fullscreen Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters Ceuta showed just how easy it is to divide Europe Paul Taylor The migrant influx prompted recriminations and a tit-for-tat dispute between Italy and Spain. Putin, Erdoğan and others will have taken note W ithin hours of the first pictures of tens of thousands of migrants swimming the short distance from Morocco to the Spanish north African enclave of Ceuta hitting social media on 30 July, 22 European Union leaders , the Trump administration and Israel had piled on to criticise Madrid. The outbreak of hysteria and recrimination was a case study in 21st-century politics, driven by real-time images in a media echo chamber where populists set the agenda on migration, propagating fear, prejudice and demagogic proposals.

stories.title: « Le français fait désormais partie du patrimoine intellectuel, scientifique et culturel de l’Algérie »
stories.summary: Un collectif d’intellectuels et de citoyens algériens ou issus de la diaspora s’inquiète, dans une tribune au « Monde », de la marginalisation progressive du français au profit de l’anglais, davantage pour répondre à des considérations idéologiques qu’à une véritable stratégie linguistique cohérente.

stories.title: RDC : un début de décrispation politique, avant un dialogue national ?
stories.summary: Quelques signaux faibles laissent penser à un moment de détente du pouvoir après que le président, Félix Tshisekedi, s’est dit ouvert à l’organisation d’un dialogue national.

stories.title: Bruno Foucher, l’ambassadeur de France en Centrafrique, visé par une procédure disciplinaire du Quai d’Orsay
stories.summary: Le diplomate a fait venir dans ses appartements privés de la résidence une trentaine de jeunes femmes entre janvier 2024 et mars 2026, poussant les services de protection à signaler une faille de sécurité, selon « Le Canard enchaîné ». Il reconnaît avoir eu des relations sexuelles avec deux d’entre elles.

stories.title: Un mariage à 20 millions de dollars, symbole du clientélisme au Zimbabwe
stories.summary: Le président et tous les membres du gouvernement, ainsi que les hommes les plus riches du pays, ont assisté, en mai, aux noces du fils du principal magnat du Zimbabwe et conseiller présidentiel, Kudakwashe Tagwirei.

stories.title: Au Kenya, le gouvernement veut réconcilier sa jeunesse avec l’agriculture
stories.summary: Le secteur, qui représente 22,5 % du produit intérieur brut kényan, est délaissé par les jeunes : l’âge moyen des exploitants est de 64 ans. Alors que la sécurité alimentaire du pays est en jeu, Nairobi promeut les métiers de la filière agricole.

stories.title: Why Rumors About Morocco Followed Spain’s Ceuta Migrant Surge
stories.summary: Claims swirled that Morocco, perhaps spurred by Israel and the United States, organized a recent border disaster. That unproven speculation, experts said, was exacerbated by the region’s complicated history.

stories.title: En Somalie, la moitié des enfants déplacés dans les camps du sud-ouest souffrent de malnutrition aiguë
stories.summary: La sécheresse qui sévit en Somalie a provoqué le déplacement de dizaines de milliers de personnes. Dans les camps de déplacés, l’ONG Médecins sans frontières affirme faire face à « une augmentation alarmante du nombre d’enfants mal nourris admis depuis janvier ».

stories.title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
stories.summary: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

stories.title: L'épidémie d'Ebola a fait plus de 2 000 morts en RD Congo depuis mai
stories.summary: Publicité L'épidémie d'Ebola a fait plus de 2 000 morts en RD Congo depuis mai Afrique L’épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola, qui continue de progresser en RD Congo, a fait depuis le mois de mai 2 011 morts, pour 4 381 cas confirmés, selon un dernier bilan publié par les autorités congolaises mardi 11 août. Publié le : 11/08/2026 - 13:51 Modifié le : 11/08/2026 - 13:53 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Des professionnels de santé dans un nouveau centre de traitement d'Ebola, dans le nord-est de la République démocratique du Congo, le 31 mai 2026. © Glody Murhabazi, AFP L'épidémie d'Ebola qui continue de progresser rapidement en RD Congo a fait plus de 2 000 morts et se rapproche ainsi de celle de 2018-2020, la plus meurtrière de l'histoire du pays. La RD Congo a déclaré le 15 mai, avec plusieurs semaines de retard, sa 17e épidémie d'Ebola, déjà considérée comme la plus importante de son histoire et susceptible de "devenir la plus grande jamais enregistrée dans le monde", selon Sania Nishtar, directrice de l'Alliance du vaccin Gavi. Le dernier bilan publié par les autorités sanitaires congolaises mardi fait état de 2 011 décès, sur 4 381 cas confirmés. Le cap des 1 000 décès avait été dépassé le 22 juillet.

stories.title: Au Maroc, la fin du démarchage téléphonique vers la France menace plus de 40 000 emplois
stories.summary: Une loi adoptée en France interdit toute prospection sans accord explicite du client à partir du 11 août. Elle met en danger des dizaines de milliers de salariés dans les centres d’appels marocains, largement dépendants du marché hexagonal.

stories.title: A burial row over Zambia's late president has turned its election into a hot contest
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, More than eight million registered voters have 14 presidential candidates to choose from By Dingindaba Buyoya BBC Focus on Africa ,Â Reporting from Lusaka Published 11 August 2026 A spectre is hanging over the Zambian election campaign in the shape of former President Edgar Lungu. Despite having died more than a year ago in South Africa, his body remains unburied amid a bitter dispute between President Hakainde Hichilema and the Lungu family that has sharpened political divisions. This has had a role in energising support for the opposition National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), particularly in the northern half of the country, traditional strongholds of Lungu's Patriotic Front (PF), as people see it as offering the best chance to unseat the incumbent. Meanwhile, it has complicated the second-term bid of Hichilema and his United Party for National Development (UPND), which draws its core support from the south, west and north-west while seeking to expand its reach nationwide. The political battle is playing out on the streets of the capital, Lusaka.

stories.title: « Ebola se propage à une vitesse que nous n’avions encore jamais observée » : l’alerte de Jean-Jacques Muyembe, codécouvreur du virus
stories.summary: Le virologue congolais, qui a mis au jour le virus en 1976, revient, dans un entretien au « Monde », sur l’actuelle propagation de l’épidémie due à Ebola en République démocratique du Congo. En seulement trois mois, le nombre de morts s’approche du bilan humain de l’épidémie de 2018, qui avait duré vingt-deux mois.

stories.title: Migrant Crisis Reveals Vast Differences Between Ceuta and Its Moroccan Neighbor
stories.summary: Ceuta, Spain, and Fnideq, Morocco, are physically separated by only a mile, but they are intertwined by family and trade. A recent border crisis is the latest chapter in their story.

stories.title: En Libye, Haftar fragilisé après l'assassinat du chef des renseignements de l'Est
stories.summary: Publicité En Libye, Haftar fragilisé après l'assassinat du chef des renseignements de l'Est Afrique Fauzi al-Mansouri, le chef des services de renseignement de l'armée de l'Est en Libye, a été assassiné lundi dans un attentat à la voiture piégée à Benghazi. Il s'agit d'une des premières attaques visant un aussi haut responsable de la région orientale depuis une dizaine d'années. Un coup dur pour le clan du maréchal Haftar, qui aspire à un contrôle total du pays. Publié le : 12/08/2026 - 01:00 Modifié le : 12/08/2026 - 08:27 5 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Le maréchal Khalifa Haftar le 16 novembre 2021 à Benghazi. © Abdullah Doma, AFP Le chef des services de renseignement de l'armée de l'Est en Libye , dirigée par Khalifa Haftar , a été tué, lundi 11 août, dans un attentat à Benghazi , un coup dur pour ce puissant clan qui aspire à contrôler tout le pays. Le commandement de l'Armée nationale libyenne (ANL) a annoncé dans un communiqué en pleine nuit la mort dans un attentat à la voiture piégée du chef militaire Fauzi al-Mansouri, l'un des plus importants du pays, fustigeant un "acte lâche et criminel".

stories.title: Les étudiants marocains touchés de plein fouet par la hausse des frais d’inscription en France
stories.summary: Un décret, pris le 19 mai, restreint les possibilités d’exonération des droits d’inscription différenciés pour les étudiants non européens. Parmi eux, les Marocains sont les plus nombreux à étudier dans les facultés françaises.

stories.title: La Guinée demande à la France la restitution du crâne de Bokar Biro, résistant à la colonisation française
stories.summary: Conakry entend récupérer les crânes du dernier souverain de l’Etat théocratique du Fouta-Djallon et de trois de ses proches, près de cent trente ans après leur assassinat par les troupes coloniales françaises.

stories.title: Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho
stories.summary: Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films View image in fullscreen Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films Review Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese pairs his literary-grade voiceover with propulsive, prophetic images to interrogate his identity and that of his colonialism-carved homeland H ere is a captivating stream of consciousness film about exile, roots and identity by Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese, director of the lauded 2019 activism story This Is Not a Burial, It’s a Resurrection . It’s ostensibly a cine-memoir looking back from the vantage point of present-day Berlin to his upbringing in Lesotho, narrated by Mosese’s dense, literary-grade voiceover. But there’s something propulsive and prophetic about the accompanying hyper-vivid images from rural and urban life.

stories.title: Evidence that South African special forces murdered top detective shared with BBC
stories.summary: Image source, Mathipa family Image caption, Lt Col Frans Mathipa was a respected detective and father of five By Yeshiel Panchia ,Â Dino Mahtani Â and Â Nick Norman-Butler ,Â BBC Eye Investigations Published 10 August 2026 Senior police detective Frans Mathipa had been fighting for four months to gain access to a crucial piece of information in the case he was working on. Finally, he was told, it was going to come his way. But he feared his pursuit of it could cost him his life. Two days later, his car was found overturned - he had been shot dead while driving. Now seven members of South Africa's special forces, and one military police officer, have been charged with murdering Lt Col Mathipa, a highly respected officer, in August 2023.

stories.title: Le pape Léon XIV appelle à l’ouverture de couloirs humanitaires au Soudan
stories.summary: « J’exhorte la communauté internationale à soutenir les efforts visant à instaurer un cessez-le-feu immédiat », a déclaré le souverain pontife, au sujet d’un conflit qui a fait des dizaines de milliers de morts et déplacé des millions de personnes.

stories.title: Au Sénégal, le long combat des héritiers d’El-Hadj Omar Tall pour le retour du « trésor de Ségou » pillé sous la colonisation
stories.summary: Le guide spirituel soufi, dont les disciples se comptent par centaines de milliers, était un érudit et un combattant anticolonialiste du XIXᵉ siècle. L’adoption par la France, en avril, d’une loi sur les restitutions des biens culturels volés pourrait permettre à ses descendants de récupérer ses manuscrits, bijoux et biens de valeur.

stories.title: Nigeria's mass wedding - and how telling lovers from fraudsters is proving tricky
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, All the new wedding outfits are paid for by the Kano state government By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 9 August 2026 Celebrations have turned the northern Nigerian city of Kano into a riot of colour and excitement over the last week as 1,500 couples married at a mass wedding. For days the city's streets have been buzzing with bridal parties and their families preparing outfits and attending other organised events. On Friday, brides in red hijabs with grooms in matching red hats and white robes went to the palace of the Emir, the city's traditional Muslim leader, for the main ceremony where they officially became husband and wife. The nuptials culminated on Saturday with a wedding breakfast hosted by Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, who offered his blessing to the newlyweds. The Kano state government sponsored this initiative, spending 1.5bn naira ($1m; Â£815,000) to support those tying the knot - providing the bride's dowry and furniture for the couple's first home.

stories.title: ‘We have no tents or blankets’: Ceuta migrants struggle to survive brutal heat and freezing nights
stories.summary: A woman from Morocco and other migrants wait and sleep in the open in Ceuta, Spain, on Thursday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters View image in fullscreen A woman from Morocco and other migrants wait and sleep in the open in Ceuta, Spain, on Thursday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters ‘We have no tents or blankets’: Ceuta migrants struggle to survive brutal heat and freezing nights Authorities wrestle with fallout from mass border crossing, as tense Spanish enclave fears it will happen again Along the wide avenues and tree-lined plazas of Ceuta’s centre, there were few hints of the recent events that catapulted the Spanish enclave on the north African coast into global headlines. But less than a mile away from the bustling bars and restaurants, at the nearby El Trampolín beach, the lingering impact was impossible to ignore. “We’re sleeping here on the beach, out in the open, without tents or blankets,” said Imad, 26, one of several thousand people believed to be still in Ceuta after last week’s extraordinary influx of more than 72,000 migrants into the Spanish territory on the edge of Morocco . “We don’t have bathrooms,” added the Yemen national. “I barely manage two hours of sleep, as it’s incredibly cold by the sea at night, and during the day the heat is unbearable.” View image in fullscreen A man prays inside a makeshift mosque marked out with stones on El Trampolín beach in Ceuta, where hundreds of migrants have been sheltering. Photograph: Okba Mohammad One week on, while questions continue to swirl over what exactly prompted the incident, the city’s shops and markets have reopened and many of the 84,000 residents have resumed their daily routines.

stories.title: Their African Islands Were Set to Be Decolonized. Then the U.S. Bombed Iran.
stories.summary: The inhabitants of the Chagos Islands were expelled by the British 60 years ago. Refugees were anxious to return this year, but their hopes have been caught in a morass of geopolitics.

stories.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
stories.summary: The checks, which come ‘amid the persistent irregular migration pressure’ facing Italy, will starts at midnight on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Sempere/AP View image in fullscreen The checks, which come ‘amid the persistent irregular migration pressure’ facing Italy, will starts at midnight on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Sempere/AP Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta. The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy , will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement. Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

stories.title: Judge approves Trump effort to end South Sudan TPS protections
stories.summary: Temporary Protected Status holders along with union leaders and advocates rally at the supreme court on 29 April 2026.
